pattern: Multiple rapid small-value transactions across different merchant categories within a 10-minute window, followed by one large withdrawal.
risk_notes: Classic card-testing pattern where a stolen card is validated with small purchases before a large fraudulent withdrawal.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Card blocked, chargeback issued, case referred to card network.

pattern: Wire transfer to a newly added beneficiary in a high-risk jurisdiction, initiated minutes after a password reset.
risk_notes: Password reset immediately followed by high-value outbound wire is a strong account takeover signal.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Account locked, transfer reversed where possible, customer notified.

pattern: Series of structured cash deposits each just under the $10,000 reporting threshold across multiple branches in one week.
risk_notes: Deposits deliberately kept under CTR threshold across branches is a textbook structuring/smurfing pattern under AML rules.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, SAR filed.

pattern: Transaction from a device and IP address never previously associated with the account, geolocated in a different country than the customer's home address.
risk_notes: New device + new geography combined is a moderate-risk signal, especially without a corresponding travel notification.
resolution: Flagged for step-up authentication. Customer verified travel; case cleared.

pattern: Sudden spike in transaction volume for a merchant account previously processing low, stable volumes, with several disputed chargebacks in the same week.
risk_notes: Sharp volume spikes combined with chargeback clustering often indicate a compromised or complicit merchant account.
resolution: Merchant account suspended pending investigation.

pattern: Repeated failed login attempts followed by a successful login and an immediate change to contact email and phone number.
risk_notes: Credential stuffing followed by contact info changes is a precursor to locking the real owner out before further fraud.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Contact changes reverted, account secured, customer notified via out-of-band channel.

pattern: Round-dollar wire transfers sent to multiple beneficiaries who share the same registered address.
risk_notes: Multiple beneficiaries at one address receiving round-dollar transfers is consistent with a money mule network.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, beneficiary accounts flagged network-wide.

pattern: Customer transaction matched a name on a periodically updated sanctions watchlist during real-time screening.
risk_notes: Any positive sanctions list match requires an immediate hold and manual compliance review regardless of transaction size.
resolution: Transaction held, compliance review confirmed false positive due to common name; released after manual clearance.

pattern: Customer's mobile number was ported to a new carrier, and within an hour the online banking password was reset using an SMS code and a large transfer was sent to an external account.
risk_notes: SIM swap gives the fraudster control of SMS one-time codes; a number port immediately before a password reset is a high-confidence takeover signal.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Account frozen, transfer recalled, customer re-verified in branch and moved to app-based authentication.

pattern: Login from a new browser followed by addition of a new payee, an increase to the daily transfer limit, and a maximum-limit transfer, all within 15 minutes.
risk_notes: Limit increase plus new payee plus max transfer in one short session is a classic takeover cash-out sequence.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Session terminated, payee removed, funds partially recovered from receiving bank.

pattern: Customer's mailing address and email were changed online, and a replacement debit card was requested to the new address two days later.
risk_notes: Contact change followed by a card reissue to the new address is used to intercept physical cards after taking over the profile.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Card cancelled before activation, contact details restored, customer notified by phone on file.

pattern: Successful login after a password reset, followed by several balance checks and a transfer to a beneficiary added in the same session, from an IP associated with a known proxy service.
risk_notes: Anonymizing proxy plus fresh beneficiary after a reset strongly indicates a compromised account.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Account locked, outbound wire stopped before settlement.

pattern: Dozens of declined one-dollar authorization attempts on different card numbers from the same merchant terminal within minutes.
risk_notes: High-velocity low-value attempts across many cards at one terminal points to a compromised or fraudster-controlled merchant used for card testing.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Terminal blocked, affected card numbers reissued.

pattern: Card used for three small online donations to unrelated charities, then for a high-value electronics purchase shipped to a freight forwarder.
risk_notes: Small charity payments are a common way to test stolen cards before a resellable purchase shipped to a forwarding address.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Order cancelled with merchant, card blocked and reissued.

pattern: Several small subscription sign-ups on a newly issued card, followed by gift card purchases totalling over $2,000 the next morning.
risk_notes: Gift cards are a preferred cash-out route because they are fast and hard to trace after a card has been validated.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Gift cards voided where possible, chargeback filed.

pattern: Customer made nine cash deposits between $8,500 and $9,800 at ATMs over five days, then wired the combined balance overseas.
risk_notes: Repeated deposits just under the reporting threshold followed by a consolidated outbound wire is consistent with structuring and layering.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, SAR filed, account placed under enhanced monitoring.

pattern: Several different individuals deposited cash just below $10,000 into the same business account on the same day at different branches.
risk_notes: Multiple depositors splitting cash into one account is classic smurfing designed to avoid currency transaction reports.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, SAR filed.

pattern: Customer repeatedly purchased money orders in amounts under $3,000 at different branches and deposited them into one account.
risk_notes: Money orders kept under recordkeeping thresholds and consolidated into one account is a structuring variant.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, SAR filed.

pattern: Login from a device never seen before, located in another state, with a correct password but failed security questions.
risk_notes: New device plus failed knowledge-based questions suggests the password may be compromised.
resolution: Flagged for step-up authentication. Customer could not be reached; account restricted until verified.

pattern: Mobile app login from an emulator rather than a physical phone, with device fingerprint changing on every session.
risk_notes: Emulators with rotating fingerprints are used to evade device-based fraud controls.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Device fingerprints blocklisted, account secured.

pattern: Customer logged in from a new country during a holiday period, and the travel notice on file matched the destination.
risk_notes: Geography change is explained by a matching travel notice, so the risk signal is weak.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared. No action required.

pattern: Newly onboarded online merchant processed a high volume of transactions in its first week, mostly from cards issued abroad, with average ticket size far above its stated business type.
risk_notes: Mismatch between stated business and actual card mix and ticket size suggests transaction laundering or a bust-out merchant.
resolution: Merchant payouts held, account suspended pending investigation.

pattern: Merchant refunded many transactions to cards different from the ones originally charged.
risk_notes: Refunds to different cards move money out of the merchant account and are a known merchant fraud technique.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Merchant terminated, refunds reversed, case referred to card network.

pattern: Restaurant merchant's daily card volume tripled overnight with most transactions keyed in manually instead of swiped or tapped.
risk_notes: Manual key entry at a card-present merchant is a sign of stolen card numbers being run through the terminal.
resolution: Merchant account suspended, investigation found compromised terminal credentials.

pattern: Student account with low historic activity received several incoming transfers from unrelated senders and forwarded almost all funds out within 24 hours.
risk_notes: Rapid in-and-out movement through a low-activity account is a strong money mule indicator.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, account closed, customer interviewed and identified as a recruited mule.

pattern: Customer received a large deposit described as a job payment, then sent most of it to cryptocurrency exchanges in several smaller transfers.
risk_notes: Fake job schemes recruit mules to receive funds and convert them to crypto.
resolution: Escalated to AML compliance, SAR filed.

pattern: Several newly opened accounts shared the same phone number and device, each receiving and forwarding similar amounts.
risk_notes: Shared device and phone across accounts indicates a coordinated mule network controlled by one operator.
resolution: Accounts frozen, network linked and reported, SAR filed.

pattern: Account received transfers from three customers who had each reported romance scams, then forwarded funds abroad.
risk_notes: Receiving proceeds from known scam victims is direct evidence of mule activity.
resolution: Account frozen, funds returned to victims where possible, SAR filed.

pattern: Outbound wire listed a beneficiary bank in a comprehensively sanctioned country, routed through an intermediary bank.
risk_notes: Routing through an intermediary does not remove sanctions exposure; transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions require a hold.
resolution: Transaction blocked and reported to compliance as required.

pattern: Customer name partially matched a sanctions list entry with a different date of birth and nationality.
risk_notes: Partial name matches need manual review; differing date of birth and nationality usually indicate a false positive.
resolution: Reviewed by compliance, confirmed false positive, transaction released.

pattern: Payment to a company whose registered owner matched an entity on a sanctions list.
risk_notes: Entities owned by sanctioned parties can themselves be subject to sanctions and require a hold.
resolution: Transaction held, compliance confirmed ownership link, funds blocked and reported.

pattern: Trade finance payment referenced shipping goods to a port in a sanctioned region, although the beneficiary was not listed.
risk_notes: Sanctions risk can come from goods, vessels or destinations, not only from listed names.
resolution: Escalated to sanctions compliance, enhanced due diligence requested before release.

pattern: New account opened with a Social Security number issued recently but a date of birth showing the applicant is 40 years old, with a credit file only a few months old.
risk_notes: Mismatch between SSN issuance and age plus a thin, new credit file is typical of synthetic identities.
resolution: Application declined, identity referred to fraud prevention team.

pattern: Customer built good credit over 18 months with small balances, then maxed out all credit lines in one week and stopped paying.
risk_notes: Long nurturing followed by a sudden bust-out is the classic synthetic identity monetization pattern.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Accounts charged off and identity flagged across products.

pattern: Several applications used the same address and phone number but different names and Social Security numbers.
risk_notes: Shared contact details across different identities indicates fabricated or manipulated identities.
resolution: Applications declined, linked identities blocklisted.

pattern: Customer disputed several online purchases as unauthorized although device, IP and delivery address matched the customer's own history.
risk_notes: Disputes on transactions that match the customer's own device and address suggest friendly fraud.
resolution: Dispute denied with evidence, account noted for future dispute review.

pattern: Customer deposited a large check, withdrew most of the funds the same day, and the check was returned as drawn on a closed account.
risk_notes: Withdrawing funds before a check clears and the check bouncing indicates deliberate deposit fraud.
resolution: Account closed, loss sent to recovery.

pattern: Elderly customer sent a large wire to a new payee after receiving a phone call from someone claiming to be the bank's fraud department.
risk_notes: Impersonation of the bank to make the customer move money to a safe account is a common authorized push payment scam.
resolution: Payment recalled with partial recovery, customer educated, case reported.

pattern: Customer paid a deposit for a rental property to a new account after seeing an online listing, then reported the landlord unreachable.
risk_notes: Fake rental listings pressure victims into paying deposits before viewing the property.
resolution: Recall request sent to receiving bank, receiving account reported as a mule.

pattern: Customer sent several transfers to an investment platform promising guaranteed returns, increasing amounts each week.
risk_notes: Escalating transfers to a high-return investment platform are a sign of an investment scam.
resolution: Customer contacted, further payments stopped, case reported.

pattern: Elderly customer's account showed large cash withdrawals accompanied by a new person who did most of the talking at the branch.
risk_notes: A third party directing transactions and unusual cash withdrawals by an elderly customer indicates possible exploitation.
resolution: Branch escalated to protective services, account placed under review.

pattern: A recently added joint account holder on an elderly customer's account began transferring funds to their own account.
risk_notes: New joint holders moving funds out is a recognized pattern of elder financial abuse.
resolution: Transfers restricted, customer interviewed privately, case referred to adult protective services.

pattern: Business customer changed a supplier's bank details after an email request, then paid a large invoice to the new account.
risk_notes: Bank detail changes requested only by email, without verification by phone, are the core of business email compromise.
resolution: Payment recalled, partial recovery, customer advised to verify changes by phone.

pattern: Finance employee received an urgent email appearing to come from the CEO asking for a confidential wire to a new overseas account.
risk_notes: Urgency, secrecy and a new beneficiary in an executive request are typical of CEO-impersonation fraud.
resolution: Wire stopped before release after callback verification failed.

pattern: Customer's payroll account was updated to route an employee's salary to a new bank following an email from a lookalike domain.
risk_notes: Payroll diversion through spoofed emails is a common business email compromise variant.
resolution: Payroll change reversed, employee paid correctly, domain reported.

pattern: Customer received refunds for returned items more than 20 times in two months, with returned packages found to contain different, cheaper goods.
risk_notes: Repeated refunds with swapped items indicate organized refund abuse.
resolution: Refunds stopped, merchant account flagged, customer banned by merchant.

pattern: Customer claimed non-delivery on many online orders although tracking showed delivery with signature at the customer's address.
risk_notes: Repeated item-not-received claims contradicted by delivery evidence point to refund fraud.
resolution: Claims denied, customer flagged for future dispute review.

pattern: Customer deposited checks between two of their own accounts at different banks repeatedly before either cleared.
risk_notes: Moving checks between banks to inflate balances before clearing is check kiting.
resolution: Accounts restricted, losses recovered, case referred to recovery.

pattern: Mobile deposit of a check that had already been deposited at another bank the previous day.
risk_notes: Depositing the same check at two institutions is a duplicate presentment fraud.
resolution: Second deposit reversed, customer warned.

pattern: Customer's online banking was accessed shortly after the customer reported a phishing text message about a locked account.
risk_notes: Phishing links that capture login credentials are a common takeover entry point.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Password reset, devices revoked, small unauthorized transfer reversed.

pattern: New payee added and immediately paid from an account whose owner was hospitalized according to a recent note on file.
risk_notes: Activity on the account of a customer known to be unavailable suggests misuse by someone else.
resolution: Confirmed fraud. Payment recalled, account secured, family contacted through authorized representative.

pattern: Large wire to a new beneficiary abroad initiated by a customer purchasing a home overseas, with supporting documents provided before the transfer.
risk_notes: High-value international wire to a new payee looks risky, but documentation and normal login behavior support legitimacy.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared. Wire released.

pattern: Small business deposited cash just under $10,000 once a week, consistent with its daily sales records over several years.
risk_notes: Deposits near the threshold are explained by a stable, long-running business pattern, not deliberate structuring.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared. Pattern documented for future reference.

pattern: Customer reset their password after forgetting it and then paid their regular monthly bills to existing payees.
risk_notes: A password reset alone is not suspicious when followed only by routine payments to known payees.
resolution: No action required.

pattern: Customer bought groceries at their usual store, in line with past spending, from their regular phone and home location.
risk_notes: Activity fully matches the customer's established behavior.
resolution: No action required.

pattern: Spike in card transactions abroad while the customer was on a business trip that matched a travel notice on file.
risk_notes: Foreign spending is explained by documented travel.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared.

pattern: Customer's name matched a common name on a sanctions list, but date of birth, address and nationality all differed.
risk_notes: Name-only matches with different identifiers are common false positives in sanctions screening.
resolution: Reviewed by compliance, confirmed false positive, released.

pattern: Merchant's sales volume increased sharply during a holiday season, consistent with the previous year's seasonal pattern.
risk_notes: Seasonal peaks that repeat year over year are expected and not a fraud indicator.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared.

pattern: Customer sent money to a new payee who was a family member, confirmed by the customer during a callback.
risk_notes: New payee risk is mitigated by successful out-of-band confirmation with the customer.
resolution: Reviewed and cleared.

pattern: Customer logged in from a new phone after upgrading their device and completed step-up verification successfully.
risk_notes: A new device is expected after an upgrade when strong verification succeeds.
resolution: No action required.
